scope: All 476 expansion records; editorial footnotes screened for explicit composition-date possibilities outside 1837–1843 despite XML safe_within_period.
methodology: Searched every editorial footnote for dates and dating language, then fully read the bodies and notes of substantive candidates. Historical publication, death, travel, and later-return dates were not treated as composition dates.

conflicts.finding: Genuine editorial-period conflict. The footnote says the letter might belong to any Shrewsbury visit from summer 1841 through November 1848, so the XML-safe July 1841 bound is not a complete composition-date possibility. The body’s Saturday/Shrewsbury close does not uniquely resolve the visit.
conflicts.proposed_conservative_hold: Retain raw XML bounds and mark date as unresolved; do not promote to exact July 1841. Consider an editorial possibility extending through November 1848 for chronology review, while keeping it outside the 1837–43 selection unless separately authorized.

evidence.quote: Believe me | My dear Sir | Yours very faithfully | Charles Darwin. Saturday
A few days since I was struck by the difference in aspect of a Cynoglossum

conflicts.footnote_evidence: This letter might have been written during any Shrewsbury visit from the summer of 1841 to November 1848.

conflicts.finding: No outside-period conflict. “Before end of 1839?” is an unresolved date within the XML year, and the footnote’s questionnaire timing is also within 1839. It does not license a pre-1837 or post-1843 composition date.
conflicts.proposed_conservative_hold: Retain the existing 1839 bound and uncertainty; do not replace it with an exact day or infer date from the later 1846 reference.

evidence.quote: at pointer bitch belonging to Chas Wilkins Esq. Hay, Breconshire
The breed had been in the family for generations

conflicts.footnote_evidence: The date is conjectured from the date at which the Wilkins family adopted the name de Winton ... The information was probably for the chapters on variation under domestication.

screened_non_conflicts.reason: 1844 is a historical death date in a footnote, not a possible composition date.
Falconer’s 1847 return to India and 1843 memoir date contextualize the 1842–43 editorial range; neither supplies an outside composition possibility.
The 1840–77 range is already represented in the ambiguous record and its footnote explains institutional endpoints; not XML-safe.
The 1842–45 or 1855–68 alternatives are already ambiguous_period, not safe_within_period.
The 1882 upper bound is already ambiguous_period and footnote reasoning supports a post-July-1843 lower bound, not safe-period overreach.

issues.issue: XML July 1841 is narrower than the explicit editorial possibility through November 1848.
Questioned “before end of 1839?” remains within the selected period; it is uncertainty, not an outside-period conflict.

verdict: One genuine safe-record editorial period conflict found (631); 13803 is a within-period uncertainty. Preserve raw metadata and maps; this report is advisory only.

quote_validation.method: Exact quote substrings checked against the fully read expansion records.
